Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core aim: “Hard‑wire fairness” into national life by redistributing power and opportunity. Four priorities:
- Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- A fair chance for every child
- A fair future by creating green jobs and rebuilding the economy
- A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring civil liberties

Tax and public finances
- Raise the income tax personal allowance to £10,000 (c. £700 cut for most; 3.6m taken out of tax), funded by: basic-rate tax relief on pensions only; equalising capital gains with income tax; anti‑avoidance; per‑plane duty to replace Air Passenger Duty; 1% mansion tax above £2m; reform non-dom status.
- Credible deficit plan: over £15bn identified annual savings; start cuts from 2011–12 based on economic tests; £400 cap on public-sector pay rises for two years; restrict tax credits; scrap ID cards/biometric passports; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; prison reform; reduce bureaucracy; review Trident and public sector pensions; better IT procurement; establish a cross‑party Council on Financial Stability.

Economy and jobs
- Break up banks (separate retail/investment), introduce a Banking Levy, reform bonuses, get lending going, grow local/regional finance (Local Enterprise Funds, Regional Stock Exchanges).
- One‑year green stimulus to create 100,000 jobs: shipyard upgrades for offshore wind, £400 “eco cash‑back” for home upgrades, public‑building insulation, bring 250,000 empty homes into use, bus scrappage; large youth opportunity programme; 15,000 extra Foundation Degrees; support apprenticeships.
- Create a UK Infrastructure Bank to mobilise private capital for energy and transport; invest in superfast broadband; reform business rates to site-value, devolve to councils; focus RDAs on economic development or replace with local authority leadership.
- Back mutuals/co‑ops; convert Northern Rock to a building society; secure Royal Mail investment with majority public/employee ownership and Post Office in public hands.

Education and skills
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium for disadvantaged pupils to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one tuition; SEN assessments for all 5‑year‑olds; stronger teacher training; anti‑bullying.
- Slim down curriculum and testing; independent standards authority; combine academic/vocational routes via a General Diploma; allow 14–19 study at college; close FE/school sixth-form funding gap.
- Phase out university tuition fees over six years (final-year fees scrapped immediately); national bursary scheme; merge skills/HE funding quangos.

Health and care
- Protect frontline NHS by cutting waste: halve the Department of Health; scrap SHAs; cap top pay; integrate health and social care; expand talking therapies; prioritise dementia research; tackle alcohol harm; improve air quality.
- Patient entitlements replace central targets; staff control ward budgets; elected Local Health Boards; GP choice and email access; language/competence tests for doctors.

Families, consumers and pensions
- Shareable parental leave; fathers’ antenatal time off; extend flexible working to all; strengthen child protection and youth services.
- Restore earnings link for state pension (triple-lock style), end forced annuitisation at 75, scrap compulsory retirement ages; respite for carers; long-term care commission.
- Fairer energy tariffs with cheapest rates for essential use; social tariffs; PostBank; cap unfair bank and card charges; cut rail fares (RPI–1%), refunds for rail replacement; regulate wheel‑clamping.

Climate, environment and transport
- Zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; 40% of electricity non‑carbon by 2020 (majority offshore/marine); efficiency drive; block unabated coal; oppose new nuclear; European Supergrid; strengthen EU ETS and push EU 30% 2020 target; protect forests; zero‑waste strategy; expand access to countryside; double woodland by 2050.
- Invest in rail reopenings and capacity; empower councils to regulate buses; promote cycling/walking; replace APD with per‑plane duty; cancel Heathrow third runway; zero‑emission cars target by 2040; prepare revenue‑neutral road pricing; rural fuel discount.

Crime, justice, immigration
- 3,000 more police funded by axing ID cards; elected police authorities; cut red tape; evidence‑led drugs policy; focus on organised crime.
- Presumption against short sentences; restorative justice; prisoners work and pay victims; move addicts/mentally ill to appropriate settings; cancel mega‑prison programme.
- Firm but fair immigration: reinstate exit checks; National Border Force; regional points‑based system; crack down on rogue employers; prioritise deporting criminals; earned regularisation for long‑resident law‑abiding migrants (pre‑2010); humane asylum with independent agency; end child detention; allow asylum seekers to work.

Politics and civil liberties
- STV for Commons (reduce MPs by ~150); votes at 16; fixed terms; stronger Commons scrutiny; fully elected second chamber; written constitution via citizens’ convention; cap donations at £10k; right to recall MPs; lobbyist register; extend FOI.
- Freedom Bill: regulate CCTV; curb council surveillance; protect jury trial and protest; reform libel; scrap ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint; limit DNA retention to convicts; end blanket retention of internet/email data; scrap control orders; 14‑day pre‑charge limit; allow intercept evidence.

International
- Meet 0.7% aid by 2013 in law; new finance (e.g., financial transaction tax); crack down on tax havens/corruption; support debt cancellation.
- Strategic defence review; no like‑for‑like Trident replacement; strengthen European defence cooperation; improve forces’ pay and housing.
- Pro‑EU reform agenda; future in/out referendum on fundamental change; euro only by referendum when conditions allow.
- Ethical foreign policy: inquiry into torture/rendition; arms trade controls; diplomacy on Iran; support two‑state solution and end Gaza blockade; Afghanistan strategy tied to governance and regional diplomacy to bring troops home during the Parliament.
</text>
